question: Complete: ___ ag foghlaim Gaeilge.
explanation: Tá mé ag foghlaim Gaeilge means “I am learning Irish.” The progressive construction uses tá + ag + verbal noun.

question: Complete: Is ___ mé. (I am a teacher.)
explanation: Is múinteoir mé is a standard way to say “I am a teacher.”

question: How do you say “I have a book”?
explanation: Irish expresses possession with tá + thing + ag + person: Tá leabhar agam.

question: Complete: Tá an cat ___ an chathaoir. (The cat is on the chair.)
explanation: Ar means “on”. Ar an gcathaoir means “on the chair”.

question: Which is a common Irish greeting?
explanation: Dia duit is a common way to say “hello”. Oíche mhaith means “good night”, and slán means “goodbye”.

question: Complete: Chuaigh mé ___ an siopa. (I went to the shop.)
explanation: Chuig can mean “to” or “towards” and introduces a destination.

question: How do you say “I am tired”?
explanation: Tá tuirse orm is a common expression meaning “I am tired”, literally “tiredness is on me”.

question: Complete: ___ sé anseo anois. (He is here now.)
explanation: Tá is the present form of bí. Bhí is past tense, and beidh is future tense.

question: How do you say “She speaks Irish”?
explanation: The usual word order is verb + subject + object: Labhraíonn sí Gaeilge.

question: Complete: Tá siad ag ___ peile. (They are playing football.)
explanation: After ag in this progressive construction, use the verbal noun: ag imirt.

question: How do you say “We went home”?
explanation: Chuaigh is the past-tense form of téigh, meaning “to go”. Abhaile means “home” when describing movement towards home.

question: Complete: D’ith mé ___. (I ate the apple.)
explanation: An t-úll means “the apple”. The t- is used before a vowel after the singular definite article.

question: How do you say “I don’t understand”?
explanation: Ní thuigim means “I don't understand”. The verb form is lenited after ní.

question: Which means “I am going home now”?
options: Tá mé ag dul abhaile anois.
explanation: Ag dul abhaile means “going home”. Sa bhaile means “at home”, while inné means “yesterday”.

question: How do you ask “Where are you?”
explanation: Cá bhfuil tú? asks about someone's location. Cad means “what” and cé means “who”.

question: Complete: ___ is ainm duit? (What is your name?)
explanation: Cad is ainm duit? is a common way to ask someone's name.

question: Which is a common response to “Go raibh maith agat”?
explanation: Fáilte romhat is a common response meaning “you're welcome”.

question: Complete: Tá cupán tae ___ an mbord. (There is a cup of tea on the table.)
explanation: Ar an mbord means “on the table”. The form of the noun changes after the preposition and article.

question: How do you say “I like music”?
explanation: Is maith liom expresses liking. Literally, it means something like “music is good with me”.

question: Complete: Ní maith ___ caife. (I don't like coffee.)
explanation: Ní maith liom means “I don't like”. Liom is part of this expression.

question: Choose the sentence meaning “The children are playing.”
explanation: The progressive construction uses tá + subject + ag + verbal noun.

question: Complete: Bhí mé ___ an bhaile inné. (I was at home yesterday.)
explanation: Sa bhaile means “at home”. Bhí is the past form of bí, and inné means “yesterday”.

question: How do you say “I saw the woman”?
explanation: Chonaic mé means “I saw”. Chonaic an bhean mé would mean “The woman saw me”.

question: Complete: Tá dhá ___ agam. (I have two cats.)
explanation: The noun after dhá is commonly lenited: dhá chat, “two cats”.

question: Which means “the books”?
explanation: Leabhair is the plural of leabhar, and na is used with plural definite nouns.

question: Complete: Tá mé níos ___ inniu. (I am better today.)
explanation: Níos fearr means “better”. Fearr is the comparative form of maith.

question: How do you say “She is older than me”?
options: Tá sí níos sine ná mé.
explanation: Níos sine ná means “older than”. Ná introduces the comparison.

question: Complete: Tá am ___ . (You have time.)
explanation: Agat means “at you” and is used in expressions of possession: tá am agat, “you have time”.

question: How do you say “I can speak a little Irish”?
options: Is féidir liom beagán Gaeilge a labhairt.
Is féidir mé labhairt Gaeilge beagán.
explanation: Is féidir liom is a common construction meaning “I can” or “it is possible for me”.

question: Complete: Ba mhaith liom ___ a ithe. (I'd like to eat something.)
explanation: Rud éigin means “something”; duine éigin means “someone”, and áit éigin means “somewhere”.

question: How do you say “I have no money”?
explanation: Níl aon airgead agam means “I have no money”. Irish expresses possession with agam.

question: Complete: Tá an leabhar ___ spéisiúil. (The book is very interesting.)
explanation: An- intensifies an adjective: an-spéisiúil means “very interesting”.

question: How do you say “I will go tomorrow”?
explanation: Rachaidh is the future form of téigh, “to go”. Amárach means “tomorrow”.

question: Complete: Nuair a ___ mé óg, bhí mé i mo chónaí sa Ghaeltacht. (When I was young...)
explanation: Bhí is the past form of bí. Nuair a bhí mé óg means “when I was young”.

question: Choose the word meaning “because”.
explanation: Mar means “because”; ach means “but”, and nó means “or”.

question: Complete: Tá sé ag obair ___ a dheartháir. (He is working with his brother.)
explanation: Le means “with”. Lena dheartháir means “with his brother”.

question: How do you say “I gave her the book”?
explanation: Thug mé an leabhar di means “I gave her the book”. Di means “to her”.

question: Complete: Is as ___ mé. (I am from Ireland.)
explanation: Is as Éirinn mé is the standard expression for “I am from Ireland”.

question: How do you ask “What are you doing?”
explanation: Cad atá tú a dhéanamh? asks what someone is doing.

question: Which word means “here”?
explanation: Anseo means “here”; inné means “yesterday”, and amárach means “tomorrow”.

question: Which sentence expresses living somewhere for two years, continuing until now?
options: Tá mé i mo chónaí anseo le dhá bhliain.
Bhí mé i mo chónaí anseo dhá bhliain ó shin.
Tá mé i mo chónaí anseo amárach.
explanation: Le dhá bhliain can describe a situation that has continued for two years. Ó shin means “ago”.

question: Complete: Ní raibh ___ agam. (I had no choice.)
explanation: Ní raibh aon rogha agam means “I had no choice”. Aon rogha means “any choice”.

question: Which expression means “although”?
explanation: Cé go means “although”; mar means “because”, and má means “if”.

question: Complete: Tá sí níos airde ___ a deirfiúr. (She is taller than her sister.)
explanation: Ná introduces a comparison: níos airde ná means “taller than”.

question: How do you say “I would like a cup of tea”?
options: Is maith liom cupán tae anois.
explanation: Ba mhaith liom expresses “I would like”.

question: Complete: Dá mbeadh níos mó ama agam, ___ níos mó leabhar. (If I had more time, I would read more books.)
explanation: Léifinn means “I would read”. Dá mbeadh introduces a hypothetical condition.

question: Which expression means “I used to play football”?
options: Ba ghnách liom peil a imirt.
explanation: Ba ghnách liom + verbal noun expresses a habitual past action: “I used to…”.

question: Complete: Tá súil ___ go mbeidh tú ann. (I hope you'll be there.)
explanation: Tá súil agam means “I hope”.

question: Complete: ___ tá am agat, cuir glaoch orm. (If you have time, call me.)
explanation: Má means “if”; nuair means “when”, and cé go means “although”.

question: Complete: Ní hamháin go bhfuil sí cliste, ___ tá sí cineálta freisin. (Not only is she clever, but she is also kind.)
explanation: Ní hamháin ... ach ... freisin means “not only ... but also”.

question: How do you say “I am hungry” in Irish?
explanation: Tá ocras orm means “I am hungry.” Tá tart orm means “I am thirsty,” and tá eagla orm means “I am afraid.”

question: How do you say “I am thirsty” in Irish?
explanation: Tá tart orm means “I am thirsty.” Irish expresses these feelings using orm, meaning “on me.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I am tired.”
explanation: Tá mé tuirseach means “I am tired.”

question: How do you say “I am cold” in Irish?
explanation: Tá mé fuar means “I am cold.” Tá ocras orm means “I am hungry.”

question: Complete: Tá áthas ___ orm.
explanation: Tá áthas mór orm means “I am very happy” or “I have great joy.” For a more natural everyday expression, Tá an-áthas orm is also common.

question: What does “Tá brón orm” mean?
explanation: Tá brón orm literally means “sadness is on me” and is commonly used to express sorrow or say “I'm sorry.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I understand.”
explanation: Tuigim means “I understand.” Feicim means “I see,” and cloiseann/cloisim forms relate to hearing.

question: What does “Ní thuigim” mean?
explanation: Ní thuigim means “I don't understand.” The negative particle ní causes lenition in this verb form.

question: How do you say “I know” in Irish?
explanation: Tá a fhios agam means “I know.” Literally, it expresses that knowledge is known to me.

question: What does “Níl a fhios agam” mean?
explanation: Níl a fhios agam means “I don't know.”

question: Complete: ___ mise Seán.
explanation: Is mise Seán means “I am Seán.” Is is used in identification sentences.

question: How do you say “She is a teacher” in Irish?
explanation: Is múinteoir í means “She is a teacher.” The pronoun í refers to a female person.

question: How do you say “He is a doctor” in Irish?
explanation: Is dochtúir é means “He is a doctor.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “We are friends.”
explanation: Is cairde muid means “We are friends.” Cairde is the plural of cara, “friend.”

question: What does “Cá bhfuil tú i do chónaí?” mean?
explanation: Cá bhfuil tú i do chónaí? means “Where do you live?”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I live in Dublin.”
options: Tá mé i mo chónaí i mBaile Átha Cliath.
Tá mé ag dul go Baile Átha Cliath.
Tá mé as Baile Átha Cliath.
explanation: Tá mé i mo chónaí i mBaile Átha Cliath means “I live in Dublin.”

question: What does “Cad as duit?” mean?
explanation: Cad as duit? is a way to ask “Where are you from?”

question: How do you say “I am from Ireland” in Irish?
explanation: Is as Éirinn mé means “I am from Ireland.”

question: Complete: Tá mé ag dul ___ an siopa.
explanation: Tá mé ag dul go dtí an siopa means “I am going to the shop.”

question: What does “Tá mé ag teacht abhaile” mean?
explanation: Tá mé ag teacht abhaile means “I am coming home.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I am going to school.”
options: Tá mé ag dul ar scoil.
Tá mé ag teacht ón scoil.
explanation: Tá mé ag dul ar scoil means “I am going to school.”

question: What does “Tá mé ag obair sa bhaile” mean?
options: I am going home from work.
I am looking for a house.
explanation: Sa bhaile means “at home,” so the sentence means “I am working at home.”

question: Complete: Tá sí ag ___ leabhar.
explanation: Tá sí ag léamh leabhar means “She is reading a book.” The progressive uses ag plus the verbal noun.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “They are eating.”
explanation: Tá siad ag ithe means “They are eating.”

question: What does “Tá sé ag ól uisce” mean?
explanation: Tá sé ag ól uisce means “He is drinking water.”

question: Complete: Tá na páistí ag ___.
explanation: Tá na páistí ag imirt means “The children are playing.” Imirt is the verbal noun.

question: How do you say “I like music” in Irish?
explanation: Is maith liom ceol means “I like music.” Irish uses the construction is maith liom.

question: What does “Ní maith liom caife” mean?
explanation: Ní maith liom caife means “I don't like coffee.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Do you like tea?”
explanation: An maith leat tae? means “Do you like tea?”

question: Complete: Is fearr liom tae ___ caife.
explanation: Is fearr liom tae ná caife means “I prefer tea to coffee.” Ná is used in this comparison.

question: What does “Tá sé níos mó ná mise” mean?
explanation: Níos mó means “bigger” or “more,” depending on context.

question: Choose the correct Irish for “This house is small.”
explanation: Beag means “small.” Teach means “house.”

question: What does “Tá an aimsir go hálainn” mean?
explanation: Tá an aimsir go hálainn means “The weather is lovely.”

question: How do you say “It is raining” in Irish?
explanation: Tá sé ag cur báistí means “It is raining.”

question: What does “Tá sé ag cur sneachta” mean?
explanation: Tá sé ag cur sneachta means “It is snowing.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “It is sunny.”
explanation: Tá an ghrian ag taitneamh means “The sun is shining.”

question: What does “Tá sé fuar inniu” mean?
explanation: Inniu means “today,” and fuar means “cold.”

question: Complete: Chuaigh mé ___ an obair inné.
explanation: Chuaigh mé go dtí an obair inné means “I went to work yesterday.”

question: What does “D'ith mé bricfeasta” mean?
explanation: D'ith mé means “I ate.” Bricfeasta means “breakfast.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I saw him yesterday.”
explanation: Chonaic mé é inné means “I saw him yesterday.” Chonaic is the past tense of feic.

question: What does “Cheannaigh sí carr nua” mean?
explanation: Cheannaigh sí means “She bought.” Carr nua means “a new car.”

question: Complete: ___ mé abhaile go déanach.
explanation: Tháinig mé abhaile go déanach means “I came home late.” Tháinig is the past tense of tar.

question: What does “Ní dheachaigh mé amach” mean?
explanation: Ní dheachaigh mé amach means “I didn't go out.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I will see you tomorrow.”
explanation: Feicfidh mé thú amárach means “I will see you tomorrow.”

question: What does “Beidh mé ann” mean?
explanation: Beidh mé ann means “I will be there.”

question: Complete: Amárach, ___ sé ag obair.
explanation: Beidh sé ag obair means “He will be working.” Amárach means “tomorrow.”

question: What does “Ní bheidh mé sa bhaile anocht” mean?
options: I won't be at home tonight.
I wasn't at home last night.
explanation: Ní bheidh mé sa bhaile anocht means “I won't be at home tonight.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Can you help me?”
options: An bhfuil tú ag cabhrú liom?
explanation: An féidir leat cabhrú liom? means “Can you help me?”

question: What does “Caithfidh mé imeacht” mean?
explanation: Caithfidh mé imeacht means “I have to leave.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I want to learn Irish.”
options: Ba mhaith liom Gaeilge a fhoghlaim.
explanation: Ba mhaith liom Gaeilge a fhoghlaim means “I would like to learn Irish.”

question: What does “Tá orm imeacht anois” mean?
explanation: Tá orm imeacht anois means “I have to leave now.”

question: Complete: Ba mhaith liom ___ a ithe.
explanation: Ba mhaith liom rud éigin a ithe means “I would like to eat something.”

question: What does “Níl aon rud agam” mean?
explanation: Níl aon rud agam means “I have nothing.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Someone is here.”
explanation: Duine éigin means “someone.” Rud éigin means “something.”

question: What does “Tá rud éigin mícheart” mean?
explanation: Rud éigin means “something,” and mícheart means “wrong.”

question: Complete: Tá an leabhar ___ an mbord.
explanation: Tá an leabhar ar an mbord means “The book is on the table.”

question: How do you say “The cat is under the table” in Irish?
options: Tá an cat ar an mbord.
Tá an cat os cionn an bhoird.
explanation: Faoin mbord means “under the table.”

question: What does “Tá an banc in aice leis an stáisiún” mean?
options: The bank is near the station.
The bank is inside the station.
The bank is behind the station.
explanation: In aice le means “beside” or “near.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “The dog is in the garden.”
options: Tá an madra ar an ngairdín.
explanation: Sa ghairdín means “in the garden.”

question: What does “Tá an siopa os comhair an tí” mean?
options: The shop is behind the house.
The shop is in front of the house.
The shop is inside the house.
explanation: Os comhair means “in front of.”

question: Complete: Tá an carr idir an teach agus ___ scoil.
explanation: Idir an teach agus an scoil means “between the house and the school.”

question: What does “Tá mo mhála liom” mean?
explanation: Mo mhála means “my bag,” and liom means “with me.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Her name is Máire.”
explanation: Is é Máire a hainm is a standard way to say “Her name is Máire.” A hainm means “her name.”

question: What does “Tá beirt deartháireacha agam” mean?
explanation: Deartháireacha means “brothers,” and beirt is used when counting people.

question: How do you say “I have one sister” in Irish?
explanation: Tá deirfiúr amháin agam means “I have one sister.”

question: What does “Is liomsa an leabhar seo” mean?
explanation: Is liomsa an leabhar seo means “This book is mine.”

question: Complete: Seo ___ cara.
explanation: Seo mo chara means “This is my friend.” Mo causes lenition, so cara becomes chara.

question: What does “Cé leis an peann seo?” mean?
explanation: Cé leis? asks “Whose is it?”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I gave him the book.”
explanation: Thug mé an leabhar dó means “I gave him the book.”

question: What does “Fuair mé bronntanas” mean?
explanation: Fuair mé means “I got” or “I received.” Bronntanas means “present” or “gift.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Please sit down.”
explanation: Suigh síos, le do thoil means “Please sit down.”

question: What does “Éirigh suas!” mean?
explanation: Éirigh suas means “Stand up!” or “Get up!”

question: How do you say “Come in” in Irish?
explanation: Tar isteach means “Come in.” Téigh amach means “Go out.”

question: What does “Fan nóiméad” mean?
explanation: Fan means “wait” or “stay,” and nóiméad means “minute.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Be careful!”
explanation: Bí cúramach means “Be careful.”

question: What does “Ná bí buartha” mean?
explanation: Ná bí buartha means “Don't worry” or “Don't be worried.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “Don't touch that!”
explanation: Ná bain leis sin means “Don't touch that!”

question: What does “Labhair níos moille, le do thoil” mean?
explanation: Níos moille means “more slowly.”

question: How do you say “Could you repeat that?” in Irish?
options: An bhféadfá é sin a rá arís?
explanation: An bhféadfá é sin a rá arís? means “Could you say that again?”

question: What does “Cad is brí leis sin?” mean?
explanation: Cad is brí leis sin? means “What does that mean?”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I speak a little Irish.”
explanation: Labhraím means “I speak,” and beagán means “a little.”

question: What does “Tá mé ag iarraidh Gaeilge a chleachtadh” mean?
options: I am trying to practise Irish.
explanation: Tá mé ag iarraidh ... a chleachtadh means “I am trying/wanting to practise ...”

question: Complete: Is féidir liom ___ Gaeilge.
explanation: Is féidir liom labhairt Gaeilge is intended to mean “I can speak Irish.” More idiomatically, say Is féidir liom Gaeilge a labhairt.

question: What does “Tá mé ag foghlaim gach lá” mean?
explanation: Gach lá means “every day.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I read the newspaper every morning.”
options: Éistim leis an nuachtán gach maidin.
explanation: Léim means “I read” in the present tense. Gach maidin means “every morning.”

question: What does “Éist liom” mean?
explanation: Éist liom means “Listen to me.”

question: Complete: Tá mé ag caint ___ mo mháthair.
explanation: Tá mé ag caint le mo mháthair means “I am talking to my mother.”

question: What does “Tá mé ag smaoineamh ort” mean?
explanation: Tá mé ag smaoineamh ort means “I am thinking about you.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I agree with you.”
explanation: Aontaím leat means “I agree with you.”

question: What does “Ní aontaím leat” mean?
explanation: Ní aontaím leat means “I don't agree with you.”

question: Complete: Tá mé sásta ___ an toradh.
explanation: Tá mé sásta leis an toradh means “I am happy with the result.”

question: What does “Tá díomá orm” mean?
explanation: Tá díomá orm means “I am disappointed.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I am proud of you.”
explanation: Tá mé bródúil asat means “I am proud of you.”

question: What does “Tá imní orm faoi” mean?
explanation: Tá imní orm faoi means “I am worried about” something.

question: Complete: Cé go bhfuil sé ag cur báistí, ___ mé ag dul amach.
explanation: Cé go bhfuil sé ag cur báistí, tá mé ag dul amach means “Although it is raining, I am going out.”

question: What does “Má bhíonn am agam, cabhróidh mé leat” mean?
options: If I have time, I will help you.
I helped you when I had time.
I don't have time to help you.
explanation: Má bhíonn am agam, cabhróidh mé leat means “If I have time, I will help you.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I stayed at home because I was sick.”
options: D'fhan mé sa bhaile mar bhí mé tinn.
Chuaigh mé amach mar bhí mé tinn.
Fanfaidh mé sa bhaile mar tá mé sláintiúil.
explanation: D'fhan mé sa bhaile means “I stayed at home,” and mar means “because.”

question: What does “Sula dtéann tú, glaoigh orm” mean?
options: If you leave, don't call me.
explanation: Sula means “before,” and glaoigh orm means “call me.”

question: Choose the correct Irish for “I have never been to Galway.”
options: Ní raibh mé riamh i nGaillimh.
Tá mé i nGaillimh gach lá.
explanation: Ní raibh mé riamh i nGaillimh means “I have never been to Galway.”

question: What does “Tá súil agam go bhfeicfidh mé thú arís” mean?
options: I hope I will see you again.
I know I saw you yesterday.
I don't want to see you again.
explanation: Tá súil agam means “I hope,” and go bhfeicfidh mé thú arís means “that I will see you again.”
